name: Amperesand Pte. Ltd. (UEN 202318356C, incorporated 11 May 2023; US subsidiary Amperesand Inc., Delaware, formed 6 December 2024)
headquarters: Singapore (Solid State Systems Innovation Center, Harbourlink Innohub); San Francisco, California (Power Electronics Innovation Center); Reno, Nevada (Design and Advanced Manufacturing Center)
employees: ~130+ (Wolfspeed case study, May 2026); 154 listed on LinkedIn and 51 open roles (Sept 2026); 38% of the global workforce in Reno per the Nevada GOED filing (Feb 2026)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Amperesand is the platform challenger at the 800 V DC hall edge — a 3.3 kV silicon-carbide medium-voltage solid-state transformer built from 200 kW modules to 4–10 MW, with a decade of NTU-lineage grid testing behind it, USD 122M of reported equity, a Reno production line running from mid-2026 and a Port of Singapore charging pilot as its first commercial engagement — but as of 19 September 2026 it has no confirmed energised unit, no named data-center customer, no certification listing and no place on any NVIDIA 800 V DC roster; whether the '30MW of commercial systems' promised for 2026 ships by year-end is the whole thesis. BACKGROUND. Spun out of Nanyang Technological University's Energy Research Institute in 2023 (Amperesand Pte. Ltd., incorporated 11 May 2023; US subsidiary Amperesand Inc., Delaware, December 2024), incubated by Temasek's Xora Innovation and first company selected for the SGD 75M Temasek–NTU–NUS programme. Research from 2016 produced a 50 kW Generation 0 (2019), 500 kW and 1.5 MW Generation I units on the Singapore grid (2022), full-power and bidirectional testing of Generation 2 (2024) and 18 patent families. Funding per company releases and trade press: USD 12.45M seed (February 2024, Xora and Material Impact), USD 80M Series A (November 2025, Walden Catalyst Ventures and Temasek) and a USD 30M share issuance reported in June 2026 (N47 Services about USD 13.5M; no company statement). Operations in Singapore, San Francisco and Reno; about 130–155 staff. Leadership turned over twice in a year: Xora's Phil Inagaki (interim CEO) to Schneider veteran Gary Lawrence (January 2025) to ex-Tesla Brian Dow (CEO by October 2025), the last change unannounced. Collection gap: no datasheet, revenue, valuation, backlog, MW delivered or shipped-unit figure is published; the company's headline claims were cut from 'up to 10x' faster time to power and '>80%' footprint reduction to '5×' and '50%' in the August 2026 site refresh without explanation.
ecosystemRole: We assess Amperesand as the second venture-backed challenger in the hall-edge power-conversion layer beside Heron Power — a modular 3.3 kV SiC solid-state transformer sold against the transformer-rectifier units NVIDIA's 2027 halls use and against the hedged incumbents (ABB, Eaton, GE Vernova, Hitachi Energy, Siemens, Schneider) — distinguished by a multi-application platform (megawatt port charging, storage, data halls) that accumulates field hours across markets, Singapore engineering with a Nevada line, and Temasek on the cap table. It is not a battery, switchgear or rack-power vendor; its adjacency to in-hall power is that the battery on its DC bus takes the UPS's job.

productsAndServices.name: Amperesand SST — medium-voltage solid-state transformer platform (third generation) for 800 V DC AI factories
productsAndServices.description: A factory-built medium-voltage solid-state transformer that takes utility medium voltage and delivers regulated low-voltage DC — the company's homepage calls it 'the world's most advanced Medium Voltage Solid State Transformer' and lists '>98.5% MV-to-LV conversion efficiency', '99.999% uptime via proprietary redundancy', '5× faster time to power' and '50% smaller equipment footprint', with 'configurable MV AC and LV DC' output 'designed for global 800V DC AI factory architectures'. The Wolfspeed case study (May 2026) describes it as 'the first medium voltage SST-to-rack power solution capable of providing 5-10MW of modular power conversion for the emerging 800 VDC AI compute ecosystem', built on 3.3 kV Wolfspeed WolfPACK full-bridge modules with Gen 4 SiC MOSFETs in the medium-voltage front end, liquid-cooled to a module temperature rise below 30°C for operation above 50°C ambient, with power stages 'small and light enough for simple two-person replacement in minutes' and modules swappable 'in less than 20 minutes'. The unit consolidates the line-frequency transformer, switchgear, rectifiers and UPS of the conventional chain into one enclosure — up to two units ship in a single 20-foot flat-rack container per the company's Nevada filing — and its DC bus lets customers 'replace uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems with lower cost, multi-sourced battery energy storage'. Third-party PCIM 2026 reporting adds the figures the company does not publish: 10–34.5 kV input, 800 V DC or 1,500 V DC output, 200 kW modules scaling to 10 MW, fanless fluid cooling, IP65, about 22 weeks from order to delivery.
highlights: Claims moderated in the August 2026 site refresh: the November 2025 Series A release, the legacy careers site and NTU say 'up to 10x' faster time to power and 'greater than 80%' footprint reduction; the current homepage says '5×' and '50%', and Wolfspeed's May 2026 release says 'over 50%'. No company document explains the change (analysis: the newer figures are the ones to quote).

Unit rating is stated three ways: '6MW SST platform' demonstrated late 2024 (January 2025 release), '6+ MW' system engineering (Wolfspeed release, May 2026), and '5-10MW of modular power conversion' (Wolfspeed case study); PCIM reporting gives 200 kW modules 'up to 10 MW'. The company publishes no datasheet, so per-unit MW, dimensions and DC output voltages rest on third-party trade-show reporting (collection gap).

Lifetime is claimed as 'designed and testing to demonstrate 15+ year lifetime' (case study), 'engineered for a 20-30-year lifetime' (Wolfspeed release) and '20 years design life' (PCIM) — unreconciled figures; the underlying claim is Wolfspeed's epoxy-package power-cycling data ('5X improvement' over silicone-gel modules).

Standards are targets, not listings: job postings name UL 2877 and UL 1741 as 'the primary standards governing Amperesand's products', with IEEE 1547, IEEE 2800, IEC 62443 and IEC 61850 supporting, and NRTL engagement with TÜV, UL, CSA and Intertek; no certification has been announced (collection gap). The homepage says 'UL, IEC & IEEE — certifying to procurement standards'.

Safety and grid features per the case study: 'settable ultra-fast shutdown of energy delivery to reduce arc flash incident energy', ability to 'safely decouple MV and LV grids', 'grid ride through, ramp rate control, and demand response', and a software suite 'from predictive maintenance to site-level asset visibility'; the Nevada filing adds that the design 'eliminates harmful materials such as SF6 gas' and 'requires no water input'.

Commercial status: 'now accepting orders for pilot deployments' (Wolfspeed PDF, May 2026); 'First commercial units delivering 2026' and 'Initial hyperscaler deployments in 2026' (homepage, August 2026); no shipped unit, energised pilot or named data-center customer is on the public record as of 19 September 2026.
productsAndServices.positioning: Sits at the medium-voltage-to-800 V DC hall-edge block that NVIDIA's August 2026 execution paper builds first from transformer-rectifier units and reserves for 34.5 kV-direct SSTs 'toward 2029'. The company names no competitor and compares only against 'legacy UPS/transformer systems'; the peer set at this layer is Heron Power (34.5 kV, 4.2 MW, mass production late 2027), DG Matrix, and the hedged incumbents — GE Vernova, ABB, Eaton, Siemens, Hitachi Energy, Schneider Electric — plus Sungrow's EnerNeo and Zhonhen's rectifier architecture. Amperesand's differentiators, as the record supports them, are a decade of NTU-lineage development with grid-tested Generation 0–2 hardware (50 kW in 2019, 500 kW and 1.5 MW in 2022, full-power and bidirectional testing of Generation 2 in 2024), a 3.3 kV SiC front end that roughly halves the series cell count of a 1.7 kV design, and a US production line in Reno; it is absent from NVIDIA's published 800 V DC partner rosters, which Heron Power is on (analysis).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct: the site's 'Talk to sales' form and product-management roles that 'engage directly with hyperscalers, colocation providers, and data-center design-build firms'; partnering with 'battery providers' for DC-side integration; a service organisation (field service, commissioning, spares, warranty, 'MSAs, LTSAs, or availability-guarantee agreements') was being stood up from scratch under a Head of Service posting in September 2026. No EPC, OEM or distributor channel is named.
targetSegments: AI factories — hyperscalers and 'Fortune 100' data-center operators (initial deployments stated for 2026)
Colocation providers and data-center design-build firms
Critical industry — ports and heavy industrial sites (PSA Singapore pilot)
Defense (named in the Series A release)
productsAndServices.roadmap: '30MW of commercial systems to be delivered in 2026 to hyperscale AI data center and critical power customers' and 'first commercial units in early 2026 to the Port of Singapore' (Series A release, November 2025); 'deploying its Medium Voltage SSTs to Fortune 100 customers in 2026' (homepage, August 2026); Reno operations start July 2026 with 62 FTE and USD 18.7M of equipment within two years (Nevada GOED application, February 2026); 'manufacture 500MW of solid-state transformer technology within the next five years' (CEO letter to GOED); 'Gen 5 in development for Utility application' (homepage). Superseded: 'first units to the U.S. and Singapore in 2025' (seed release, February 2024).

productsAndServices.name: Amperesand SST for megawatt charging and port electrification
productsAndServices.category: Medium-voltage EV and port charging conversion
productsAndServices.description: The same platform configured for megawatt-class DC charging: the seed-stage description was 'compact, modular, intelligent, bidirectional units for DC fast-charging, microgrids, data centers', shipping as 'containerized SSTs with customizable mixed AC/DC output' in '2, 4, and 6MW units, scalable by combination' (TDK Ventures, February 2024). The first commercial engagement is PSA International: a one-year proof of value at PSA Singapore's electric prime-mover charging, agreed through PSA unboXed in October 2024 and targeted to start mid-2025, with 'first commercial units in early 2026 to the Port of Singapore, supporting a mission critical charging pilot' per the Series A release. The legacy site describes the platform as 'configurable to support a range of applications including megawatt charging and 800V DC AI Factory power', and PCIM 2026 reporting lists 'port power/shore power' among the use cases.
highlights: This is the application on which the technology was proven before AI: a 1.5 MW system tested on the Singapore grid closed a seven-year NTU validation programme (seed release), and the 2024 pilot programme at Singapore's port is the first entry on the company's own timeline after launch.

Bidirectional operation is a stated property — 'full-power, overload, and bidirectional testing' of Generation 2 completed in 2024 — which is what a charging depot needs for vehicle-to-grid and what a battery block needs for charge and discharge.
No PSA unit has been confirmed delivered or energised; the 'early 2026' commitment is unverified on either party's channels as of September 2026 (collection gap).
productsAndServices.positioning: Competes with the conventional depot chain (step-down transformer, low-voltage switchgear, per-charger rectifiers) and with the handful of SST-for-charging entrants (WattEV's in-house MV-PCS for truck charging; Delta and ABB's charging-side power). The port use case is a reliability proving ground rather than the revenue story (analysis).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to port operators and fleet owners; PSA engagement structured as a proof of value through PSA unboXed.
targetSegments: Port and terminal operators electrifying prime movers and automated guided vehicles
Heavy-duty truck and bus depots (Megawatt Charging System class loads)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Port of Singapore first commercial units 'early 2026' (Series A release); no further charging-market roadmap published after the November 2025 release, and the August 2026 homepage lists ports under 'Critical Industry' without a date.

productsAndServices.name: Amperesand SST for storage, microgrids and the grid (Generation 5 in development)
productsAndServices.description: The platform's on-grid/off-grid capability — 'supports both on-grid and off-grid environments' with 'AI-native power controls' (Series A release), 'rapid on/off grid switching' and 'large load management … in constrained grid environments' (homepage) — is marketed for storage integration and constrained-grid sites, and the homepage lists a 'Gen 5 in development for Utility application'. The Wolfspeed case study frames the DC bus as the way customers replace UPS with 'lower cost, multi-sourced battery energy storage' and cites 'grid ride through, ramp rate control, and demand response'.
highlights: No storage or utility product name, rating or customer is published; the utility generation exists only as a homepage roadmap line (collection gap).
Job postings cite IEEE 1547 and IEEE 2800 interconnection standards and 'medium-voltage (5 kV to 36 kV) systems', consistent with a distribution-connected grid product.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Not yet sold; direct engagement with 'utility customers' is stated on the legacy site.
targetSegments: Battery storage integrators pairing DC blocks with the SST bus
productsAndServices.roadmap: 'Gen 5 in development for Utility application' (homepage, August 2026); no date.

recentDevelopments.headline: Hiring for a Head of Service to stand up field service, commissioning, spares and warranty from scratch, and a Director of Product Compliance naming UL 2877 and UL 1741 as the governing standards
recentDevelopments.read: A service organisation and a compliance lead being recruited in September 2026 date the certification and support work to the present, not the past — consistent with no listing and no energised fleet on the record (analysis).

recentDevelopments.headline: Website relaunch: leadership roster now Dow (CEO), Joyner (SVP Engineering), Reznik (CFO), Bouchet (Chief of Staff); headline claims moderated from 'up to 10x' faster time to power and '>80%' footprint reduction to '5×' and '50%'; 'deploying … to Fortune 100 customers in 2026'
recentDevelopments.read: The claims were halved without explanation as first deliveries approached; the newer figures are the ones a buyer will be shown and the ones this dossier quotes.

recentDevelopments.headline: New York Times Magazine feature on a national blackout scenario visits the Reno pilot line, where 'CEO Brian Dow is building a modular solid-state alternative aimed first at AI data centers'
recentDevelopments.read: Mainstream coverage of the transformer shortage is now the company's most visible profile; it says nothing about a shipped unit.

recentDevelopments.headline: NVIDIA, Google and Microsoft publish the 800 V DC execution paper and the OCP LVDC Solid-State Transformer Specification v0.3 with 'more than 80 equipment manufacturers'; Amperesand is not named, while Heron Power, DG Matrix, Delta, Eaton, ABB, Siemens, Hitachi Energy and GE Vernova are named across the October 2025, GTC 2026 and August 2026 rosters
recentDevelopments.read: Third consecutive NVIDIA roster without the company; the CEO's statement that Amperesand sits on five of seven OCP working groups is self-reported and the specification's contributor list could not be read.

recentDevelopments.headline: Power Electronics News CEO interview publishes the fullest specification on record: 10–34.5 kV in, twin 800 V outputs (series for 1,500 V), 200 kW galvanically isolated power stages, 4–10 MW systems, N+X with automatic bypass, IP55 enclosure, sub-25-week lead time, Wolfspeed 3.3 kV baseplate-less modules; pilots named as Port of Singapore, STT GDC and 'hyperscale AI customers'; standards UL 2877 and IEEE 3105
recentDevelopments.read: The only near-datasheet in the public record is an interview; a buyer still cannot download a rating table.

recentDevelopments.headline: PCIM Europe 2026 (Nuremberg): modular SiC SST shown — 10–34.5 kV input, 800 or 1,500 V DC output, 98.5% single-stage efficiency, 200 kW modules to 10 MW, fanless fluid cooling, IP65, ~22 weeks order to delivery, 20-year design life; SiC sourcing breadth cited as Infineon, STMicroelectronics and Wolfspeed; 'a single pilot installation is underway at a Singapore port'
recentDevelopments.read: The first European trade-show appearance pitches lead time against 'one-year-plus' conventional units and names the EU 2030 shore-power mandate as a second market.

recentDevelopments.headline: USD 30M 'fresh share issuance from new and existing investors', with N47 Services contributing about USD 13.5M (DealStreetAsia; Hyphen Partners) — no company release; databases label it Series A-II and total funding USD 122.45M
recentDevelopments.read: A quiet extension seven months after the Series A, by a Singapore-registered investor vehicle rather than a headline lead, reads as bridge capital toward first deliveries (analysis); the company's only acknowledgement is the About page's '>$100M'.

recentDevelopments.headline: SemiAnalysis '800VDC Revolution' names Amperesand (>98.5%) with DG Matrix, Heron Power and Novos Power as the SST vendor set, sizes a 2030 SST market of ~USD 32B at USD 1.25M/MW, and cautions that SSTs 'lack field reliability data at datacenter scale and require active cooling'
recentDevelopments.read: Independent analyst recognition of the vendor set, with the reliability caveat that applies to every name on it.

recentDevelopments.headline: Wolfspeed launches 3.3 kV WolfPACK modules with Amperesand as the named design-in — 'engineering of a 6+ MW medium voltage solid-state transformer system', 'over 50% footprint reduction', '20-30-year lifetime' — and co-publishes a case study ('5-10MW of modular power conversion', 99.999% uptime, <20-minute module swap, 'now accepting orders for pilot deployments')
recentDevelopments.read: The silicon supplier is the company's most detailed public advocate; the dependence on one post-Chapter 11 supplier's 3.3 kV part is the supply-chain risk the same document creates.

recentDevelopments.headline: NTU 'Built to scale' profile: research from 2016, 150 kW proof-of-concept then a 1 MVA containerised demonstrator, Generation 2 full-power, overload and bidirectional testing completed 2024, NRF Central Gap Fund with NTU, ERI@N core team moved to the company in 2024, 'expects to exceed 100 employees worldwide in 2026'
recentDevelopments.read: The university's account of the lineage is the best evidence for the 'ten years of development' claim and is more modest than the '6MW platform' language of the January 2025 release.

recentDevelopments.headline: Reno, Nevada selected for the US manufacturing facility at 9735 Double R Blvd — 73,000 sq ft, USD 18.4M of equipment, 'more than 60 new jobs over the next two years' at USD 55.50 average hourly wage, USD 2,004,004 of state abatements, power-stage manufacturing on site, operations from July 2026
recentDevelopments.read: A modest fit-out rather than a gigafactory: enough to build pilot and early commercial units, not the 500 MW-a-year the CEO's letter aspires to (analysis).

recentDevelopments.headline: Nevada GOED board approves performance-based abatements for Amperesand Inc.; the application (signed 31 October 2025 by Brian Dow as 'Chief Executive Office / Co-Founder') commits 62 FTE in two years, 110 within five, USD 18,684,000 of investment, and states a plan to 'manufacture 500MW of solid-state transformer technology within the next five years'
recentDevelopments.read: The only externally enforceable numbers the company has published; the milestone slide dates the first hyperscaler data-center and Port of Singapore deliveries to Q2 2026 — neither confirmed since.

recentDevelopments.headline: STT GDC launches the FutureGrid Accelerator at NTU's Jurong Island campus — 'Southeast Asia's first live HVDC-powered AI infrastructure testbed', developed with LITEON and supported by ERI@N and Amperesand, validating at least 325 kW; STT GDC 'plans to deploy this technology in future data centres in Singapore'
recentDevelopments.read: The first data-center operator engagement on the record is a sub-megawatt testbed with an NVIDIA-listed rack-power partner, in the company's home market.

recentDevelopments.headline: USD 80M oversubscribed Series A co-led by Walden Catalyst Ventures and Temasek; new investors Industry Ventures, Acclimate Ventures, SG Growth Capital; '30MW of commercial systems to be delivered in 2026', first commercial units 'in early 2026 to the Port of Singapore', 'multiple additional 2026 commercial pilots secured' with hyperscale AI customers, headcount to exceed 100 by year-end
recentDevelopments.read: The largest pure-play SST startup raise of 2025 (mgrid) and the round that dated every 2026 commitment this dossier now tracks.

recentDevelopments.headline: Brian Dow signs the Nevada incentive application as 'Chief Executive Office / Co-Founder' — the earliest dated document showing him as CEO after Gary Lawrence's January 2025 appointment; Marc Bouchet joins as Chief of Staff from TDK Ventures (October 2025)
recentDevelopments.read: The company's second CEO change in a year went unannounced; Lawrence's exit has no date or reason on the record, and the Schneider/ABB grid-incumbent profile he brought has been replaced by a Tesla energy-products profile (analysis).

recentDevelopments.headline: NVIDIA publishes its 800 V DC ecosystem partner list at the OCP Global Summit — nine facility-tier power providers including Heron Power — without Amperesand
recentDevelopments.read: The roster that defines the hall-edge peer set for hyperscaler buyers omitted the company at the moment it was closing its Series A on that very thesis.

recentDevelopments.headline: Canary Media's SST survey notes Amperesand's units 'being tested on Singapore's power grid' alongside DG Matrix and Resilient Power (acquired by Eaton that month)
recentDevelopments.read: Grid-connected testing in Singapore is the company's differentiator against paper-stage rivals; the incumbent buying a startup the same month shows how the hedged players intend to compete.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Amperesand's product is specified for NVIDIA's medium-voltage-to-800 V DC block and is not on NVIDIA's list: three consecutive rosters (October 2025, GTC 2026, August 2026) name Heron Power, DG Matrix, Delta, Eaton, ABB, Siemens, Hitachi Energy and GE Vernova at the hall edge and omit Amperesand. Basis: the NVIDIA developer blog and execution-paper coverage; the CEO's 'five of seven OCP working groups' is self-reported and the specification's contributor list could not be read. A hyperscaler pilot can proceed without a roster line, but the roster is what a buyer's design-build firm reads first (analysis).

(High confidence) We assess that no delivery commitment has been met on schedule: the PSA proof of value was 'slated for mid-2025' (October 2024), first commercial units 'early 2026' (November 2025), 'Q2 2026' for both the port and a hyperscaler (Nevada milestone slide), and 'underway' with no energisation confirmed by either party by September 2026. Basis: PSA's and the company's releases, the GOED packet and PCIM reporting. The 30 MW 2026 target is therefore back-loaded into the final quarter.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the platform argument is the company's real differentiator against Heron Power and the reason it entered through ports rather than data centers: a 200 kW cell proven at 1.5 MW on the Singapore grid and cycled daily at megawatt charging loads accumulates the fleet reliability record that a 99.999% uptime claim requires and that no data-center SST vendor yet has. Basis: NTU's account of Generation 0–2 testing, the PSA engagement, and SemiAnalysis's caveat that SSTs 'lack field reliability data at datacenter scale'. The cost is a cell rated for the worst duty cycle of three markets rather than optimised for one (analysis).

(Moderate confidence) We assess the 3.3 kV Wolfspeed design-in is both the engineering edge and the single-supplier risk: it roughly halves the series cell count of a 1.7 kV design and buys overshoot margin, and it ties the front end to one part (IBB020A33GM4) from a supplier that emerged from Chapter 11 in 2025 whose 200 mm capacity mgrid calls the sector's 'single biggest external constraint'. The company's stated second sources (Infineon, STMicroelectronics, Microchip) are unconfirmed by those suppliers.

(Moderate confidence) We assess roughly USD 122M of equity against an USD 18.7M Reno fit-out and a 130–155 headcount is sufficient to ship pilot and first commercial units but not the 500 MW-a-year line the CEO's letter describes; a Series B or a manufacturing partnership before the end of 2027 is the expected tripwire, and mgrid's judgment that the Series A is below a real medium-voltage production line's capex is the independent view. The quiet USD 30M extension by a Singapore vehicle rather than a headline lead is consistent with bridge financing (analysis).

(Low confidence) We assess the unexplained halving of the headline claims (10× → 5× time to power; >80% → 50% footprint) and the CEO turnover reflect a company moving from pitch to delivery under new leadership rather than a technical setback. No source states either; the alternative reading — that early units underperformed the pitch — cannot be excluded from the public record.

INDICATORS TO WATCH — Q4 2026: an energised unit at PSA Singapore or at a named hyperscaler (confirms the first delivery commitment; a second slip into 2027 would put the company in the 2027 TRU wave with no fleet). Any UL 2877 / UL 1741 listing (converts the standards targets into a bankable product). Any appearance on NVIDIA's GTC 2027 roster or in the OCP LVDC SST specification's contributor list (closes Judgment 1). A company statement on the June 2026 round and any Series B (tests Judgment 5). A datasheet or product page (settles the 4–10 MW, IP55/IP65, 22-versus-25-week and lifetime discrepancies). Reno headcount against the 62-FTE two-year milestone (the only externally enforceable check on the ramp).

relationships.note: Absent from every NVIDIA 800 V DC partner roster (October 2025, GTC 2026, August 2026) while building for NVIDIA's 800 V DC architecture; the CEO says the company sits on five of seven OCP working groups.
relationships.context: NVIDIA's 13 October 2025 developer blog listed nine facility-tier power providers and its rack-power and silicon partners; Power Electronics News' GTC 2026 coverage and the August 2026 execution paper again named Heron Power, DG Matrix, Delta, Eaton, ABB, Siemens, Hitachi Energy and GE Vernova at the hall edge. Amperesand appears on none, and the OCP LVDC SST specification's contributor list could not be read. Its product is nevertheless specified against that architecture ('designed for global 800V DC AI factory architectures'; twin 800 V outputs), and Wolfspeed's case study says AI-training load profiles 'jointly released by NVIDIA, Open AI and Microsoft' were used in testing — a paper reference, not a partnership.

relationships.note: The two venture-backed 34.5 kV-class hall-edge SST startups; SemiAnalysis lists both (Heron 98.5%, Amperesand >98.5%) and trade press pairs them with DG Matrix as the startups 'riding the 800VDC wave'.
relationships.context: Heron Link is a single 4.2 MW unit for data centers (and 5 MW for solar/storage) with mass production in Morgan Hill from late 2027, USD 140M Series B and a place on NVIDIA's facility-tier roster. Amperesand sells a 200 kW-module platform to 4–10 MW with a Reno line running from mid-2026, USD 80M Series A plus a USD 30M extension, and no roster listing. Neither has a confirmed energised data-center unit as of September 2026. The contest between them is schedule and fleet evidence, not efficiency, since both claim 98.5%-plus (analysis).

relationships.note: Co-developer of the STT GDC FutureGrid Accelerator HVDC testbed at NTU (January 2026), where Amperesand's SST supports the 325 kW-plus system.
relationships.context: STT GDC's release says the testbed was 'jointly developed by STT GDC and LITEON, supported by ERI@N and NTU deep-tech spinoff Amperesand'. LITEON is an NVIDIA-listed rack-power and BBU vendor, so the testbed pairs a hall-edge SST with a qualified rack shelf on a live HVDC bus — the integration a hyperscaler pilot would require. No commercial agreement between the two companies is published.

relationships.note: Named with ABB, Hitachi Energy and Siemens Energy as the incumbent SST competitors in Series A coverage; Eaton bought Resilient Power in August 2025 and is on every NVIDIA roster.
relationships.context: mgrid's Series A analysis lists 'Heron Power (modular multilevel topology), DG Matrix (multiport topology) … Eaton, ABB, Hitachi Energy, Siemens Energy' as the competitive set. Eaton's in-house SST via the Resilient Power acquisition and its 2.5 MW MV SST container for the NUS testbed (May 2026) make it the incumbent most directly overlapping Amperesand's Singapore home market; mgrid's separate claim of a 2024 '2.5 MW demonstration with Eaton at NUS' by Amperesand appears in no other source and is treated as a conflation.

relationships.note: Incumbent named in the Series A competitive set; ABB is also an investor in rival DG Matrix and holds the 34.5 kV static UPS position at the hall edge.
relationships.context: mgrid names ABB among the incumbents competing for the medium-voltage-to-DC block; TechCrunch's February 2026 survey frames the startup field as 'DG Matrix/ABB' versus 'Heron/a16z' versus Amperesand 'incubated by Temasek's early stage fund'. No commercial contact between ABB and Amperesand is published.

relationships.note: Incumbent named in the Series A competitive set; also the transformer supplier whose lead times the company's 'time to power' claim is measured against.
relationships.context: mgrid lists Hitachi Energy among the incumbent SST developers; the company's own pitch — 'reducing time to power from 24-36 months to just 100 days' (January 2025) — is a claim against the conventional transformer supply chain that Hitachi Energy leads. No commercial contact is published.

relationships.note: Named at the hall edge on NVIDIA's GTC 2026 roster from which Amperesand was absent; holds a hyperscaler's conditional commitment to buy 1,000 SSTs from 2027.
relationships.context: Power Electronics News' GTC 2026 coverage lists the SST vendors NVIDIA showcased — 'DG Matrix, Delta, ABB, Siemens, Hitachi Energy, GE Vernova, Eaton, Heron Power' — and Amperesand is not among them. GE Vernova's conditional 1,000-unit hyperscaler commitment (recorded in the Heron Power dossier) is the tier's key commercial datapoint and the incumbent order Amperesand's 'Fortune 100' pilots would have to displace (analysis).

relationships.note: Delta had a live SST deployment (Chindata/Meituan, February 2026) and is ranked with Amperesand on the vendor-authored HIITIO top-ten list; Delta also owns the rack-shelf layer an SST hands off to.
relationships.context: HIITIO's July 2026 ranking places Amperesand fourth and Delta tenth among data-center SST suppliers — a vendor-authored list that ranks its author first, cited here only as a statement that the two are seen in the same set. Power Electronics News' spotlight piece records Delta's live SST at a Chinese operator, which is the field-hour evidence no startup yet has.

relationships.note: Former CEO Gary Lawrence's eleven years as Schneider's global president of power and grid, and 'APC (now Schneider Electric)' hires cited by the company; Schneider is on every NVIDIA roster as an incumbent.
relationships.context: The January 2025 appointment release presented Lawrence's Schneider Electric and ABB record as the reason for his hiring; he left within the year, unannounced. The company's Reno team includes a 'designer of UPS systems at APC' per the Nevada filing. Schneider competes at the hall edge as one of the hedged incumbents but no direct commercial or competitive statement naming both companies exists beyond roster context.

relationships.note: Named with STMicroelectronics and Wolfspeed as the company's SiC sourcing breadth in PCIM 2026 reporting, and by the CEO as a competing 3.3 kV module supplier; Wolfspeed is the design-in.
relationships.context: all-about-industries' PCIM report says the company sources SiC from 'Infineon, STMicroelectronics, and Wolfspeed'; the July 2026 CEO interview names 'Infineon Technologies, Microchip' as the alternative 3.3 kV module suppliers to Wolfspeed. Wolfspeed (not a covered company) is the named part in the medium-voltage front end (IBB020A33GM4); Infineon's role is second-source optionality, stated by the company and not confirmed by Infineon.

relationships.note: The executive lineage: CEO Brian Dow (Powerpack/Megapack, Hornsdale, Supercharger V3, 4680 pilot) and SVP Engineering Tommy Joyner (4680 capacity, Cybertruck 400/800 V architecture, Powerwall 3) are ex-Tesla, and the Reno team is drawn from Gigafactory Nevada.
relationships.context: Company bios and the Nevada filing ('Former Tesla key lead of Gigafactory Nevada manufacturing for Model 3 … and all Tesla energy products'; NPI manager ex-Tesla) show the operating team was recruited from Tesla's energy and Nevada manufacturing organisations — the same lineage as Heron Power's founder. No commercial relationship with Tesla exists.

policyExposure.exposure: USD 2,004,004 over ten years for Amperesand Inc. — a 2% sales-tax abatement for two years (USD 1,154,890), 50% modified business tax for four years (USD 125,452) and 50% personal property tax for ten years (USD 723,662) — against commitments of 62 FTE at USD 55.50 average hourly wage within two years, 110 positions within five, and USD 18,684,000 of capital investment; GOED projects USD 13,812,135 of new tax revenue over the abatement period. The application states 80% of revenue will be generated outside Nevada and that the company will 'manufacture the power stage components of our solid-state transformers on-site'.
policyExposure.mitigation: The company sited its US design and manufacturing center at 9735 Double R Blvd, Reno, and markets the product as 'U.S.-built — with optimized supply chains'.

policyExposure.regime: Section 232 tariffs on transformers and power-conversion equipment
policyExposure.exposure: Section 232 steel-and-aluminum derivative duties were extended to transformers from 18 August 2025 (50% on non-US steel and aluminium content) and restructured by Proclamation 11021 (April 2026: power transformers under HTS 8504.21/.22 at 25% on full value; static converters and UPS under HTS 8504.40 dutied on the enclosure) — trade-press summaries that do not mention solid-state transformers or Singapore. No source addresses how an SST built partly in Singapore and partly in Reno would be classified (8504.40 versus 8504.2x) or what share of its content is US-made; Power Electronics News separately notes that higher-voltage SiC devices 'face international shipping restrictions'. The company's only statement is that its hardware 'leverages supply chains optimized for tariffs and lead times' (legacy site). Collection gap: no FEOC, domestic-content or 45X statement exists for the company.
policyExposure.mitigation: Power-stage manufacturing in Reno per the Nevada filing; the 'U.S.-built' positioning on the August 2026 site.

policyExposure.regime: UL 2877 / UL 1741 / IEEE 1547 certification for medium-voltage conversion equipment
policyExposure.exposure: Asia Business Outlook (November 2025): the company 'has not disclosed specific certification listings or independent field performance data to support its 99.999 percent uptime claim'. The company's September 2026 compliance posting names UL 2877 and UL 1741 as 'the primary standards governing Amperesand's products' with IEEE 1547, IEEE 2800, IEC 62443 and IEC 61850 supporting; the July 2026 interview adds IEEE 3105 and the OCP LVDC SST work. No listing has been announced, and SemiAnalysis (May 2026) records that no vendor had completed data-center SST certification.
policyExposure.mitigation: NRTL engagement with TÜV, UL, CSA and Intertek and a Director of Product Compliance hire, per the company's job postings.

policyExposure.exposure: PCIM 2026 reporting quotes the company that 'EU regulation mandates shore power for ships at major ports starting 2030' and that 'a single pilot installation is underway at a Singapore port for European deployment' — the port configuration's stated demand driver outside Singapore.

Analysis: roughly USD 122M of equity against an USD 18.7M Reno fit-out and a 130-plus headcount reaches first commercial deliveries; a 500 MW-a-year line will need a further raise.
